walkthroughs.body_html:
Introduction to Economics — a core area of Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Introduction to Economics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Introduction to Economics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Ricardo published 'Principles of Political Economy and Taxation' in:

options: Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
The value of the next-best alternative foregone when a choice is made — the real cost of a decision in terms of what you give up.
Opportunity cost is the total of everything you give up when making a choice.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between revenue and profit?
options: Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity); profit is what remains after deducting costs from revenue.
Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
Revenue and profit mean the same thing.

mcqs.q: What components make up aggregate demand?
options: Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
Aggregate demand is just the total amount consumers want to buy.
AD = C + I + G + (X - M): consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. A shift in any component shifts the AD curve.
Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
